findings.title: Phpinfo Use
findings.description: The phpinfo() function is used to output information about PHP's configuration, which can reveal sensitive information about the environment, such as file paths and database credentials. Removing this function call prevents potential attackers from gathering this information. This fix assumes that the phpinfo() call is not necessary for the application's functionality.
findings.cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.fix_hint: Remove the phpinfo() function call to prevent information disclosure

findings.title: Tainted Sql String
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly inserts user input into the SQL query. Using prepared statements with parameter binding ensures that user input is treated as data, not as part of the SQL code. This prevents an attacker from injecting malicious SQL code and reduces the risk of data theft or manipulation.

findings.fix_hint: Use prepared statements to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities

attack_chains.title: SQLi to RCE
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses SQL injection to extract database credentials, then uses these credentials to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec vulnerability, achieving persistence on the system. This chain requires minimal skill and results in critical data loss. The attacker starts by exploiting a SQL injection vulnerability in the low.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker extracts database credentials using SQL injection in vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php (id: 3718457c)
Step 2: attacker uses extracted credentials to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec vulnerability in vulnerabilities/exec/source/low.php (id: 45412d06)
attack_chains.remediation: Input validation and sanitization for all user-provided data in low.php to prevent SQL injection

attack_chains.title: Phpinfo to SQLi
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses phpinfo to reveal database configuration details, then uses this information to perform a SQL injection attack, potentially extracting sensitive data. This chain requires minimal skill and results in critical data loss. The attacker starts by accessing the phpinfo.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker reveals database configuration details using phpinfo in phpinfo.php (id: 805d3aed)
Step 2: attacker uses revealed database configuration to perform SQL injection in vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php (id: 3718457c)
attack_chains.remediation: Remove or restrict access to the phpinfo.php file to prevent information disclosure

attack_chains.title: SQLi to RCE via Exec
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses SQL injection to extract database credentials, then uses these credentials to gain access to the system, and finally uses a tainted exec vulnerability to achieve remote code execution, resulting in full system compromise. This chain requires moderate skill and results in critical data loss. The attacker starts by exploiting a SQL injection vulnerability in the sqli_blind/source/low.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker extracts database credentials using SQL injection in vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/source/low.php (id: 7b0af33d)
Step 2: attacker uses extracted credentials to gain access to the system and then exploits a tainted exec vulnerability in vulnerabilities/exec/source/medium.php (id: 9d0c4dd9)
attack_chains.remediation: Implement secure password storage and input validation for all user-provided data in sqli_blind/source/low.php to prevent SQL injection
